text:
devops-bot: ALERT: post-deploy latency/throughput regression detected for runtime pool 'eu-west-2/g4dn'. 95p latency jumped >3x, throughput down ~45%. Auto-mitigation recommended. (alert id: A-2026-03-15-19)

oncall-amber: saw this alert. paging eng-runtime. routing sig: @kevin-l @sophia-m

kevin-l: on it. which rollout?

lina-eng: rollout id deploy-2026-03-15-19 (kernel selection tweak + batching heuristic). canary at 15% when alert fired.

kevin-l: can reproduce on metrics:
- p95 baseline ~120ms -> now ~420ms
- throughput from 12k rps -> ~6.5k rps on that pool
- increased kernel_fallback_count in logs

kevin-l: looks like kernel affinity heuristic is flipping a bunch of pods into a fallback path with slower kernels, GV cache thrash (+ taildrop).

sophia-m: seeing eviction-loop in autoscaler logs, pods getting OOMKilled-ish? not full OOM but heavy GC + eviction of KV cache.

ops-bot: recent events:
- 2026-03-15T19:02:11Z kernel_fallback_count=312
- 2026-03-15T19:03:02Z batching_retries=47
- 2026-03-15T19:04:15Z taildrop_events=128

emily-cs: support reports increased error rate and latency for AcmeCorp and BetaRetail. priority customers affected. AcmeCorp webhook timeouts spiking.

oncall-amber: severity P1. customer-impacting. recommend immediate mitigation steps: 1) stop canary 2) revert kernel selection change or flip kill-switch 3) fallback routing to previous runtime pool

lina-eng: can cancel canary rollout: `/rollout cancel deploy-2026-03-15-19 --canary-only` — doing now.

lina-eng: cancel submitted. canary traffic rollback started.

kevin-l: parallel: enable feature-flag `runtime.kernel-selection-v2` = false in prod for eu-west-2 (kill-switch). link: https://console.redundant/flags/runtime.kernel-selection-v2

sophia-m: suggest also adjusting batching: set `batching.max_batch_tokens=256` and `batching.max_items=8` for pool to limit KV thrash. will push via config override.

kevin-l: applying batching override now.

kevin-l: also enabling temporary routing to fallback model-variant `redwood/opt-std-v1` for high-traffic routes to reduce kernel variance.

devops-bot: ACTIONS TAKEN:
- canary cancel requested by lina-eng
- flag runtime.kernel-selection-v2=off by kevin-l
- batching override applied by kevin-l
- traffic reroute to redwood/opt-std-v1: initiated

ops-bot: metric snapshot 5m after mitigations:
- p95 down from 420ms -> 180ms
- throughput recovering: 6.5k -> 9.8k rps
- kernel_fallback_count falling

emily-cs: AcmeCorp latency confirmed improving on customer side. still saw a few timed out requests during peak.

oncall-amber: good. continue monitoring. coordinate with SRE for scaling if needed.

sophia-m: noticed spike of `taildrop` messages in the logs during rollout. snippet:
```
[19:03:02] runtime: taildrop event on shard-11, kv_cache_evicted=2048, inflight=512
[19:03:03] runtime: kernel_fallback=true, selected_kernel=generic_matmul_slow
```

kevin-l: root cause hypothesis: new kernel affinity heuristic caused hot-sharding of KV caches leading to hot-evictions, causing frequent cold KV misses and fallback to generic kernels. batching heuristics amplified the churn.

lina-eng: rolling back the full deploy (not just canary) is currently on the table if we see re-rise after canary cancel finishes.

emily-cs: open CS ticket created: TKT-5421 documenting impacted customers, timeline, mitigation, and follow-up ask for notification template.

oncall-amber: handing off to night oncall @sophia-m for observation window. please capture timeline and assign postmortem.

sophia-m: taking handoff. I'll keep watching until 0400 UTC. put me on the incident channel for any customer escalations.

kevin-l: I'll prepare a revert PR for the kernel selection change and test in staging. aiming for revert + canary in 2 hours if stable.

lina-eng: also enabling autoscaler soft-limits to avoid eviction-loop: increase `kv_cache_memory_reserve` from 0.06 -> 0.12 for pool. applied.

ops-bot: post-mitigation check at +30m:
- p95 150-210ms
- error-rate back to baseline for non-high-traffic routes
- throughput ~10.5k rps (still below pre-deploy peak)

emily-cs: sending interim customer note to AcmeCorp: "We detected a performance regression after a deploy and applied mitigations; latencies improving; we will follow up with a timeline and postmortem." (drafted)

oncall-amber: good. follow-up items for postmortem:
- reproduce root cause (kernel affinity + batching)
- test kv cache pressure on canary harness
- add a pre-deploy check for taildrop rate and kernel_fallback_count
- improve kill-switch runbook to be faster (reduce manual steps)

sophia-m: assigned postmortem owners: kevin-l (root cause), lina-eng (release controls), emily-cs (customer comms).

kevin-l: noted. will include perf regression thresholds and a small e2e that simulates heavy KV churn.

oncall-amber: incident status -> mitigated but still under observation. keep this thread updated.

devops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated at 2026-03-15T19:35:00Z, observation window started.

sophia-m: leaving handoff notes in the incident doc: https://wiki.internal/incidents/1905009999 (will populate timeline).

emily-cs: leaving message for CS rotation overnight to escalate if any customer regression reappears.

lina-eng: prepping revert PR now. won't merge until we have green canary in staging.

kevin-l: thx all. I'll post an RCA stub in the incident doc once I have kernel traces.

oncall-amber: closing the active paging loop for now. keep monitoring and escalate on any regression. :white_check_mark:
